after.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{t}^{2}-12t,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-12t) \\  & =6t-12\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity is

$$
v(1)=6(1)-12=-6.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-6|=6.$

after.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in feet) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{e}^{-t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3t,\,t>0.

after.worked_solution:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =-3{e}^{-3}+\frac{3}{3}-3 \\  & =-3{e}^{-3}-2 \\  & ≈-2.15\,\text{ft/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-2.15|=2.15\,\text{ft/s}.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1).$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot 2t \\  & =\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$
